# Page 21^page=21
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 21 Daily Content PDF NATIONAL AFFAIRS NBA Notifies CMLRE & ARI as National Repositories under Biological Diversity Act, 2002 In April 2026, the National Biodiversity Authority (NBA), in consultation with the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), notified two institutions, Referral Centre Bhavasagara at the Centre for Marine Living Resources and Ecology (CMLRE) (Kochi, Kerala) and MACS Collection of Microorganisms and National Fungal Culture Collection at Agharkar Research Institute(ARI), Pune, Maharashtra, as national repositories under Section 39 of the Biological Diversity (BD Act, 2002). • Following the inclusion of these two institutions, the national network of repositories has now increased to 20, enhancing the conservation and systematic documentation of biological resources. Exam Hints: ✓ What? 2 Institutions Notified as National Repositories ✓ Designated By: NBA with MoEFCC ✓ Institutions: ✓ Referral Centre Bhavasagara at CMLRE (Kochi, Kerala) ✓ MACS Collection of Microorganisms and National Fungal Culture Collection at Agharkar Research Institute (Pune, Maharashtra) ✓ Under: Section 39, Biological Diversity Act, 2002 ✓ Total Repositories: 20 ✓ Key Role: Preservation & documentation of biological resources. About New National Repositories: Referral Centre Bhavasagara at CMLRE: It is a specialized national facility dedicated to deep-sea biodiversity, working under the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES). • At present, it maintains more than 3,500 taxonomically identified and geo-referenced voucher specimens, including invertebrates and deep-sea fishes from unexplored marine areas. MACS Collection of Microorganisms (ARI, Pune): It is a well-established facility with specialization in preserving microbial cultures. • It handles rare and difficult-to-grow microorganisms, including anaerobic and extremophilic species. National Fungal Culture Collection of India (ARI, Pune): It is a leading national repository dedicated to fungal diversity. • It is entrusted with the responsibility to maintain authenticated fungal cultures collected from diverse habitats across India. • It further supports research in fungal identification and classification. Role of National Repositories: Preservation: These repositories will ensure the safe custody of biological materials, including voucher specimens, under appropriate scientific conditions and made accessible for research and innovation in a transparent and accountable manner. Documentation: It will facilitate the documentation of newly discovered species, as well as biological resources used for research and commercial purposes.

About National Biodiversity Authority (NBA): Legal Status: It is an autonomous statutory body established under Section 8 of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002. It functions under the MoEFCC. 3-tier Structure: It operates through a three-tier structure which comprises: NBA (at national level), State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs) (at state level), and Biodiversity Management Committees(BMCs) (at local level). Key Functions: NBA performs regulatory and advisory roles for conservation, sustainable use of biological resources, and equitable benefit sharing. Chairman – Virendra Tiwari Headquarters – Chennai, Tamil Nadu (TN) Established – 2003 Amul Becomes 1st Indian FMCG Company to Hit Rs 1 Trillion Turnover in FY26 In April 2026, Anand Milk Union Limited (AMUL) became the first company in India’s Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG) sector to achieve an annual turnover of over Rs 1 lakh crore (Rs 1 trillion) in Financial Year 2025–26 (FY26), registering around 11% growth over the previous year. Exam Hint: ✓ What? Crosses Rs 1 trillion turnover ✓ When? FY26 (April 2026) ✓ Entity: Anand Milk Union Limited (AMUL) ✓ Significance: Becomes 1st Indian FMCG Company to cross Rs 1 Trillion Turnover ✓ Revenue: Rs 1 lakh crore (Group); Rs 73,450 crore (GCMMF) ✓ Other Entity: Saraswat Cooperative Bank ✓ Achievement: Crosses Rs 1 lakh crore business. About AMUL’s Milestone: Financial Performance: For FY26, the federation reported a total group turnover of Rs 1,00,000 crore, becoming the largest FMCG organisation in India. • Its marketing arm, Gujarat Cooperative Milk Marketing Federation (GCMMF), reported revenue of Rs 73,450 crore in FY26, up from Rs 65,911 crore in FY25 (11.4% growth). Product Diversification: Key growth drivers included value-added segments such as protein-rich products, organic offerings, probiotics, and high demand for buttermilk and cheese. Global Expansion: The surge was driven by Amul’s entry into international markets, including the launch of fresh milk in the United States of America (USA) and Europe, alongside a presence in more than 50 countries. Operational Scale: The milestone is supported by 3.6 million dairy farmers, 18 district cooperative unions, and a massive portfolio of over 1,200 product packs. Saraswat Cooperative Bank Crosses Rs 1 Lakh Crore Business Milestone In April 2026, Saraswat Cooperative Bank, India’s largest Urban Cooperative Bank (UCB) headquartered in Mumbai (Maharashtra), crossed the Rs 1 lakh crore total business mark, strengthening its position in the cooperative banking sector. Expansion Plans: As part of its growth strategy, the bank recently opened 8 new branches in North India and plans to add 13 more branches in the immediate future to expand its footprint beyond traditional strongholds.

Chairman – Ajay Seth Headquarters – Hyderabad, Telangana Established – 1999 SEBI grants extension for IPO approval validity, MPS norms to September 30, 2026 In April 2026, Market regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has announced a two- pronged, one-time relief measure for companies, easing both Initial Public Offering (IPO) validity timelines and Minimum Public Shareholding (MPS) compliance. • The regulator has given a temporary relaxation for companies whose IPO approvals i.e., SEBI Observations Letters expiring between April 1 and September 30, 2026 will now remain valid till September 30, 2026. • SEBI also granted a one-time relaxation for listed companies to meet the 25 per cent MPS compliance norms whose deadlines fall between April 1 and September 30, 2026. Exam Hint: ✓ What? SEBI grants relief in IPO validity and MPS compliance timeline ✓ IPO validity: SEBI extends validity for approvals expiring April-Sept 2026 ✓ MPS Compliance: Listed firms spared MPS penalties until Sept 2026 ✓ Reason: Market volatility due to West Asia conflict. SEBI issued these relaxations to help companies deal with the current uncertain market conditions caused by geopolitical tensions, especially the West Asia conflict. About IPO Extension: Conditions: As per existing regulations under the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, a public issue must be launched within 12 months under the normal route observation letter and for confidential route the validity is up to 18 months. Conflict: Due to ongoing geopolitical tensions and subdued investor participation, several issuers have faced challenges in accessing capital markets, leading to delays or withdrawal of issuance plans. Relaxation: To address this, SEBI has granted a one-time extension for observation letters expiring between April 1, 2026 and September 30, 2026. These will now remain valid until September 30, 2026. About MPS compliance Extension: Guideline: MPS means listed companies must have at least 25 per cent of their shares held by the public, not promoters, to ensure transparency and fair trading. Issue: Due to volatility and weak investor participation, many companies are finding it difficult to meet Minimum Public Shareholding (MPS) rules. Relief: Sebi has also addressed concerns of listed companies that are yet to meet minimum public shareholding requirements and directed the stock exchanges and depositories not to initiate any penal action, for those whose deadlines fall between April 1 and September 30. • Further, it also said any penalties already imposed during this period will be withdrawn. About Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI): Formation: SEBI, established on April 12, 1988, as a non-statutory body, gained full statutory powers via the SEBI Act, 1992. Chairman – Tuhin Kanta Pandey Headquarters- Mumbai, Maharashtra

Canara HSBC Life Insurance Launches Market-Linked Savings ‘Plan Promise4Wealth’ In April 2026, Canara HSBC Life Insurance Company Limited (Canara HSBC Life Insurance) launched ‘Promise4Wealth’, a next-generation Unit Linked Insurance Plan (ULIP) designed to offer long-term wealth creation along with life insurance protection. Fund Options: Policyholders will have the option to access to various funds, including a passive fund linked to the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE 500) Enhanced Value 50 Index. Background: Election: The NA elected Tô Lâm (To Lam) as President with 100% support (495/495 deputies present) in the 500-seat assembly. Shift: This development marks a shift in Vietnam’s power structure, as the roles of Party General Secretary and State President have traditionally been held by separate individuals. PM: During the same session, Le Minh Hung, former Governor of the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV), was elected as Prime Minister (PM) of Vietnam. • He succeeded Pham Minh Chinh, becoming the youngest person to hold the post. About Tô Lâm: Early Career: He began his career in public security in 1979 after graduating from the Vietnam People’s Security Academy. Security Chief: He rose through the ranks to become the Minister of Public Security in 2016, a position he held until 2024, overseeing the nation’s internal security and anti-graft efforts.
